verdict.rationale: Omarchy documents a standard ISO-to-USB install, dual booting beside Windows or other OSes on a single partition, and unattended installs. It claims to run on hardware as old as a 2011 ThinkPad X220 with 2GB RAM, and graphics drivers (including NVIDIA on supported hardware) are configured at install time. Community reports confirm quick installs on fresh machines, and one user ran it on a cheap Chromebook, though the ISO route failed there and they had to fall back to archinstall. missing for 10: an explicit hardware compatibility list or documented lock-in/portability guarantees, NVIDIA support defined beyond 'supported hardware', and evidence the ISO installs reliably on unusual hardware such as Chromebooks.
